intent.title: Make isolated test fixtures and child readiness reliable

purpose: inspection evidence; not a recovery checkpoint

risks.description: Shared source aliases, stale readiness, or premature cleanup can make parallel tests corrupt one another or falsely pass. Apply the proposal's existing preserve-and-own policy to every temporary boundary.

ownership.git_state: Disposable test outputs stay outside tracked source state; maintained helper and test source changes are tracked; the Draft remains ignored until normal completion publication.
ownership.owner_after_creation: The creating test/helper owns its fresh output; the existing isolated supervisor assumes its established cleanup responsibility after startup.
ownership.owner_during_operation: Each fixture and supervisor owns only its own writable state and launched processes; installed source dependencies and sibling fixtures remain outside that ownership.
ownership.paths: Disposable dependency copies, test roots, readiness/result markers and child-process scratch files created by these helpers.
ownership.permitted_mutation: Mutate private copies and owned markers only; preserve preexisting files and controller evidence; remove owned output only after owned children are settled, retaining failed-cleanup remnants and diagnostics under the existing policy.
ownership.upgrade_behavior: Recreate disposable state for each run without migration, cache reuse, or retention change; preserve behavior of callers that do not request readiness.
ownership.validation: Compare source and sibling sentinels, exercise actual compile and dispatch consumers, require fresh readiness and verify process termination plus cleanup error propagation.
ownership.when_exists: Reject dependency destination collisions including dangling symlinks; use fresh fixture-owned marker locations, never interpret preexisting foreign state as readiness or delete it.

scenarios.evidence: Extend the real concurrent yamerl compilation regression with linked inputs and source/peer before-and-after checks.
scenarios.given: Installed dependency sources include linked files and directories and existing build caches.
scenarios.then: Copies contain independently writable regular source data and required headers, omit dependency build caches, and produce usable compiled dependencies without changing sources or each other.
scenarios.when: Two fresh fixtures copy those sources and compile concurrently using private build paths.
scenarios.wrong_result: Copies preserve links to shared writable data, lose yamerl headers, or pass a copy assertion while the compiler consumer fails.

scenarios.evidence: Real temporary files and symlinks with sentinel comparisons; broken/cyclic link and copy-failure negative controls.
scenarios.given: A destination is an existing directory, file, valid symlink, or dangling symlink; alternatively a fresh copy encounters a broken or cyclic source link or copy failure.
scenarios.then: Existing destinations and their targets remain untouched and are rejected; invalid fresh copies fail visibly and are never returned as usable, with cleanup confined to newly owned output.
scenarios.when: The dependency fixture helper attempts the copy.
scenarios.wrong_result: Merge into a stale directory, follow a destination link, silently skip broken input, or remove preexisting data after failure.

scenarios.evidence: Real delayed/absent readiness, early nonzero exit and running-descendant timeout controls through IsolatedCase.run and the macro/run! parent consumer; include no-readiness compatibility.
scenarios.given: An isolated child starts later than the short collection window but within its separate startup bound.
scenarios.then: Startup delay does not consume the post-readiness window; missing readiness, early child exit, and post-readiness timeout produce distinct actionable failures, with bounded waits and owned children terminated before confirmed cleanup.
scenarios.when: A readiness-aware caller waits for a fresh marker from the running workload and then starts collection timing.
scenarios.wrong_result: Start collection at process launch, accept stale readiness, wait indefinitely, hide an early exit as a timeout, or return while an owned child survives.

scenarios.evidence: Extend HarnessRoleTest and check-reachable terminal controls with real child processes, pipe/PTY behavior and descendant liveness assertions.
scenarios.given: The existing fake Shaper route uses open pipe or PTY stdin and can delay startup, wait for EOF, fail, or leave background work.
scenarios.then: Valid delayed startup passes in both modes, waiting for EOF still fails after readiness, early failure and missing readiness are diagnosed, and owned process cleanup occurs on success and failure without replacing the original failure with a false pass.
scenarios.when: The terminal probe waits for child readiness and observes bounded completion through Harness.exec_shaper.
scenarios.wrong_result: Classify slow startup as waiting for stdin, close stdin to make a defective fake pass, test only a stand-in consumer, or leak children on an exceptional path.

scenarios.evidence: Preserve and run existing isolation and cleanup regressions, including real permission-denied deletion, overlap, assertion failure, abrupt exit and parent cancellation; adapt timing controls to observed readiness.

scenarios.then: Parent cwd/environment and unrelated files stay unchanged; selected tests execute once; owned children terminate before successful removal; cleanup failure remains a failing result with the retained path and cause.
